validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE, CLASSIFICATION and SPEC all confirmed by 3 independent, non-GEM origins. This is a real, completed FERC lateral: FERC docket CP09-455 (the sheet's cited wiki page names Docket CP09-455/CP09-456 nowhere directly, but the harvested citation pool's bit.ly link resolves to the BANNED abarrelfull.wikidot.com mirror -- not used). (1) EIA's official 'U.S. Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' workbook (eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/eia-naturalgaspipelineprojects.xlsx, Historical Projects tab) carries a row named 'FGT Mobile Bay Lateral Expansion' -- an exact name match to this GEM segment -- Operator 'Florida Gas Trans Co', Project Type 'Lateral', Status 'Completed', Completed Date 2011-09-22, Year In Service 2011, State(s) 'AL', Cost (millions) 34, Miles 8.9, Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) 343, Diameter (Inches) 24, Docket CP09-455 -- matching GEM's LengthKnown (8.90 mi), Diameter (24 in), Capacity (343.00 MMcf/d) and SegmentCost (34,000,000 USD) EXACTLY. (2) FERC's own Federal Register EA notice (2010-8707, docket CP09-455/CP09-456) states: 'Approximately 8.8 miles of 24-inch-diameter mainline pipeline, from near Grand Bay in Mobile County, Alabama to the existing FGT Compressor Station (CS) 44 in Mobile County, Alabama' -- confirms diameter and length (8.8 vs 8.9 mi is EIA/FERC rounding, not a discrepancy) and independently corroborates the project is real and FERC-certificated. (3) Natural Gas Intelligence (naturalgasintel.com, contemporaneous 2010 trade-press article) states FGT 'is requesting authorization to build extension facilities to transport 342,610 MMBtu/d of regasified natural gas from the proposed $1.1 billion LNG plant in Pascagoula to the existing Mobile Bay Lateral' and that 'the existing Mobile Bay Lateral runs from FGT's mainlines near Citronelle, AL, to FGT's Compressor Station 44 in Mobile Bay, AL' -- 342,610 MMBtu/d is materially the same figure as 343.00 MMcf/d (natural gas heat content ~1,000-1,050 Btu/scf), an independent (different publisher, different document class -- trade press vs. FERC notice vs. federal statistical workbook) corroboration of Capacity, and a second independent statement that the lateral is wholly within Alabama. Classification (Lateral, gas transmission, not gathering) matches EIA's own 'Project Type=Lateral' field and the FERC docket. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 37-row roster: no other FGT row (P2529 East Louisiana 0.0mi/cap75; P2594 Putnam 30.3mi/cap169; P2738 South Alabama 0.0mi/cap60; P4028-P4060, lengths 0.3-483.0mi) matches this row's 8.9mi/24in/343MMcf/d signature -- this is its own distinct, non-duplicated project. Opened and read to exhaustion: EIA workbook (Historical Projects tab, full FGT block), FR 2010 EA notice (2010-8707, full text), FR 2008 NOI (E8-30744, full text -- pre-filing dockets PF08-31/PF08-32, distinct from the eventual CP09-455 certificate docket), NGI article (full text), en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Gas_Transmission (full text, for Operator/Owner corporate-structure context). CROSS-ROW LEAD (not on the 37-row roster, so not filed as a cross_row_leads object): the FR 2010 EA notice and the NGI article both describe a companion 'Pascagoula Expansion Project' (Transco, CP09-456) of ~15.5 miles of 26-inch pipe from Jackson County, MS to Grand Bay, Mobile County, AL, ~810,000-820,000 Dth/d, delivering regasified LNG from the Gulf LNG Clean Energy Pascagoula terminal into this Mobile Bay Lateral -- no roster PID matches that signature (Mississippi is out of this batch's scope); flagging for a future Mississippi/Transco discovery pass rather than fabricating a PID match.
